metadata.triageAdvice: Seek emergency care immediately. Call emergency services or go to the nearest ER.
metadata.description: Fever combined with shortness of breath may indicate a severe respiratory condition such as pneumonia or a pulmonary embolism.

metadata.triageAdvice: Monitor symptoms closely. If fever exceeds 39°C or symptoms worsen, consult a doctor within 24 hours.
metadata.description: Fever with cough is a common presentation of respiratory infections such as influenza or COVID-19.

metadata.triageAdvice: Seek emergency care immediately. Respiratory infection with breathing difficulty requires urgent assessment.
metadata.description: A respiratory infection that progresses to shortness of breath is a high-risk escalation pattern.

metadata.triageAdvice: Rest, stay hydrated, and take over-the-counter pain relief if needed. See a doctor if headache persists beyond 48 hours.
metadata.description: A headache without fever or neck stiffness is likely a tension-type or dehydration headache with no urgent concern.

metadata.triageAdvice: Seek emergency care immediately. This combination of symptoms may indicate meningitis.
metadata.description: The triad of headache, stiff neck, and fever is a classic presentation of bacterial meningitis — a medical emergency.

metadata.triageAdvice: You have been flagged for emergency referral. Please call 999 or go to the nearest emergency department.
metadata.description: Any patient flagged with a severe respiratory risk must be referred to emergency services.

metadata.triageAdvice: You have been flagged for emergency referral. Please call 999 or go to the nearest emergency department.
